name: Sindou Peaks
region: Sindou, Léraba Province, Cascades Region · Burkina Faso
subtitle: The Sindou Peaks are weathered sandstone formations beside the town of Sindou, capital of Léraba Province, about 450 km west of Ouagadougou.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Beside Sindou, capital of Léraba Province, about 450 km west of Ouagadougou

facts.label: Geology
facts.value: Sandstone cliffs interbedded with dolerite sills, eroded into ruin-like landscapes ('aiguilles de Sindou')

facts.label: Banfora cliff
facts.value: The plateau edge between Banfora and Bobo-Dioulasso is marked by a cliff rising 150 to 200 m above the crystalline plain

facts.label: Plateau
facts.value: Precambrian sandstone plateau at an average altitude of 450-500 m in the west

facts.label: Original name
facts.value: Village originally called Sudugo, 'protection of the spirits', per a local guide

facts.label: Settlement by the Senufo
facts.value: Per oral tradition (as told by a guide), Senufo moved from southern Mali to the peaks in the 14th century

facts.label: Reason for settling
facts.value: Senufo came fleeing oppression, raids and domination

facts.label: Visitors (guide's figure)
facts.value: About 30,000 tourists a year, with lean periods since two crises, according to a guide

facts.label: Administrative location
facts.value: Sindou is chef-lieu of Léraba Province, in the Cascades region

parts.text: The Sindou Peaks are weathered sandstone formations beside the town of Sindou, capital of Léraba Province, about 450 km west of Ouagadougou. A 1975 geological survey describes sandstone cliffs interbedded with dolerite sills that have eroded into ruin-like landscapes. According to oral tradition, Senufo people from southern Mali settled among the peaks in the 14th century, and a local guide says the site draws about 30,000 tourists a year.
